r.정치 구도: A presidential system led by a directly elected president, who can serve only two terms. Democracy and decentralization took root after Suharto's dictatorship fell in 1998, but politicians from the military remain influential. With many parties, presidents run parliament through broad multiparty coalitions. It has more Muslims than any other country, but its state ideology, Pancasila, recognizes several religions. It is moving its capital from Jakarta to Nusantara on Borneo.

t.why: Southeast Asia's largest economy, with more than 270 million people, a G20 member, and home of the ASEAN secretariat in Jakarta. In the non-aligned tradition of the 1955 Bandung Conference it hosted, it tries to side with neither the United States nor China, and it joined BRICS in 2025. Next to the Strait of Malacca, it sits on the route bringing Middle East oil and European cargo to East Asia. With some of the world's largest nickel reserves for EV batteries, it bans exports of raw ore so that processing happens at home. It sometimes clashes with Chinese fishing boats and coast guard ships near the Natuna Islands in the South China Sea.
t.rel: Southeast Asia's largest country, playing the role of ASEAN's elder sibling. It has a strong non-aligned tradition of not taking sides, and in 2025 it joined BRICS, the emerging-economy group.
t.korea: The two established relations in 1973, and their Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement took effect in 2023. Korea is co-developing the KF-21 fighter jet with Indonesia, and Hyundai and LG have built car and battery plants there. With so many young people, K-pop and Korean dramas are hugely popular, and many Indonesian workers are employed in Korea.
t.know: With more than 17,000 islands and hundreds of languages, the official Indonesian language is what holds the country together. Lying on the Ring of Fire, it has frequent earthquakes and volcanic eruptions.
etext: It has the world's largest nickel reserves, and plenty of coal, palm oil, tin, copper and gold. Its coal and palm oil exports rank at the very top in the world.
By banning exports of raw nickel ore and requiring smelting at home, it drew a wave of Chinese-funded smelters. It aims to build on this to attract battery and EV plants.
With the world's fourth-largest population, its consumer market is big, and digital services such as online shopping and ride-hailing have grown fast.
Its smelting industry is criticized for relying on coal power and environmental destruction. Frequently changing regulations unsettle investors.
